questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of alternative text for images?

options.text: To improve the color contrast of an image.
To allow assistive technologies to read a description of the image aloud.
To make the image file size smaller for mobile devices.
To replace the image with text on all screens automatically.

questions.explanation: Alternative text provides a hidden description that screen readers can read aloud for users who cannot see the image.
questions.hint: Think about how a screen reader interacts with a visual element.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand the purpose of alternative text for images.

questions.prompt: According to the 2026 WebAIM Million report, how common is the issue of missing alt text?

options.text: It affects less than 10 percent of homepages.
It is rarely found on modern websites.
It affects 53.1 percent of homepages, making it the second most common failure.
It affects exactly 100 percent of websites.

questions.explanation: The 2026 WebAIM Million report shows that 53.1 percent of web homepages fail to provide alternative text for images.
questions.hint: It represents one of the most widespread accessibility failures on the internet.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize the prevalence of missing alt text across the web.

questions.prompt: How should a purely decorative image be handled?

options.text: It must have an extremely detailed description.
It should always be removed from the page completely.
It can be marked as decorative so that screen readers skip it.
It requires an accompanying audio description file.

questions.explanation: If an image adds no meaning to a page, marking it as decorative allows screen reading software to ignore it without causing confusion.
questions.hint: Consider what information is actually lost if the image is ignored.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify when an image needs description versus when it is purely decorative.
